title: AEIB v0.4.0: Bounded Synthetic Benchmark and Local Runtime Reference for Agent Effect-Integrity Evidence
description:
AEIB v0.4.0 is a bounded synthetic benchmark and execution-evidence proposal prepared for independent reproduction. It evaluates how a gateway handles state-changing agent actions when transport outcomes become ambiguous. The package binds a unique operation to an exact request, records typed transport and effect dispositions, removes retry authority after uncertain dispatch, and reconciles target state where a declared status source exists.

Track B uses a target-side ledger oracle rather than agent self-report or browser-page text as the grading source. The package includes schemas, reference harnesses, comparative artifacts, negative tamper tests, and an offline verifier. Results are reported by the producing environment. Real third-party API behavior, live TinyFish execution, universal exactly-once behavior, deployment readiness, and regulatory compliance are not established.

The package contains the scenario suites listed below; exact test counts are provided in the machine-readable manifest:
- Track B (Web-Mutation Wire Faults): 11 scenarios (B01–B11)
- Extended Edge Cases: 7 scenarios (BT12–BT18)
- Governance Boundary Tests: 11 scenarios (AT15–AT25)
- MCP Egress & Federation: 7 scenarios (AT30–AT36)
Total test cases: 36 core execution-evidence scenarios across 36 scenario IDs.

Key Deliverables:
1. aeib-bench v0.1: Synthetic benchmark evaluating agent runtime behavior against an independent target-side ledger oracle.
2. Identity Triad Specification: Separates unique intent instance (operation_id) from exact request hash (request_digest) and target idempotency identity (business_idempotency_key).
3. Prior-Art Adjusted Integration: Explicitly positioned against LIMBO (arXiv:2609.29095), RFC 9110 HTTP semantics, and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (proposing gen_ai.effect_disposition event projection).
4. AEIB Gateway Adapter and AEIB PAP Adapter Proposal: Reference control-plane adapter enforcing RFC 8785 JCS payload binding, fail-closed uncertainty latching (retry_safe: false), single-flight out-of-band target probe coalescing, real Ed25519 cryptographic receipts, and decoupled human release separation.
5. Regulated Evidence Export Reference: Supporting telemetry generation designed to inform DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) Article 17 incident timeline logs, Article 28(3) Register of Information templates (RT.01.01–RT.02.03 xBRL-CSV), EU AI Act Article 14/50 evidence workflows, and SCITT-compatible evidence architecture (RFC 9943).

Locked Milestone Claim:
Under the declared synthetic Track B scenarios, the harness matched gateway dispositions to an independent target-side ledger and issued no speculative retry in the tested ambiguous cases (11/11 reported synthetic scenarios matched the declared oracle).
